words: ولو أنما في الأرض من شجرة أقلام
rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad supplies an omitted ثابت as the predicate of أنما, inferred from the conditional construction and the particle's sense of established fact.
rows.anchor: بقرينة كون ( أن ) دالة على الثبوت والتحقق وإلى هذا ذهب المبرد

words: ولو أنما في الأرض من شجرة أقلام
rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh treats the clause as a subject that needs no overt predicate because its subject and predicate are stated afterward.
rows.anchor: وقال سيبويه : إن ذلك مبتدأ مستغن عن الخبر لذكر المسند والمسند إليه بعده

words: ولو أنما في الأرض من شجرة أقلام
rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One analysis makes the construction a subject whose predicate is estimated before it; Ibn ʿAsfur instead places the estimated predicate after it.
rows.anchor: وقيل : مبتدأ خبره مقدر قبله وقال إبن عصفور : بعده

rows.speaker: ابن عصفور
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAsfur locates the omitted predicate after the subject; the phrase ما في الأرض is the noun of أن, and من شجرة explains ما or its locative pronoun as a circumstantial phrase.
rows.anchor: و ( ما في الأرض ) أسم أن و ( من شجرة )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author parses أقلام as the predicate of أن and allows من شجرة to explain either ما or its pronoun in the locative phrase.
rows.anchor: فهو في موضع الحال منها أو منه أي ولو ثبت أن الذي أستقر في الأرض كائنا من شجرة

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan says the construction disproves al-Zamakhsharī's claim that an أن following conditional لو must have a verbal predicate.
rows.anchor: قال أبو حيان : وفيه دليل دعوى الزمخشري وبعض العجم ممن ينصر قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author answers that the alleged verb requirement applies only when the predicate is a derived adjective, so the inanimate noun أقلام and the cited nominal predicates do not refute it.
rows.anchor: وتعقب بأن إشتراط كون خبرها فعلا إنما هو إذا كان مشتقا فلا يرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Two cited poems use nominal predicates after لو أن; لو أنهم بادون is set aside because its لو expresses a wish rather than a conditional.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر : ولو أنها عصفورة لحسبتها مسومة تدعو عبيدا وأزنما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: شجرة means every tree here: an indefinite can be universal after a conditional when context calls for it, as in the cited Qurʾanic expression.
rows.anchor: والمراد بشجرة كل شجرة والنكرة قد تعم في الإثبات إذا أقتضى المقام ذلك

rows.speaker: إبن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās illustrates the force of a generic singular by answering that one date is better than one locust when asked about expiation for killing a locust in pilgrimage.
rows.anchor: وقول إبن عباس رضي الله عنهما لبعض أهل الشام وقد سأله عن المحرم إذا قتل جرادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each tree supplies many pens through its parts or branches, yielding the sense that all the trees' parts or branches become pens.
rows.anchor: وكون كل شجرة أقلاما بإعتبار الأجزاء أو الأغصان فيؤل المعنى إلى لو أن أجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular شجرة is better than أشجار or شجر because it avoids implying a distributive assignment of one pen to each tree, which would weaken the hyperbole.
rows.anchor: على أشجار أو شجر لأن الكلام عليه أبعد عن إعتبار التوزيع بأن تكون كل شجرة

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan calls this a singular indefinite used with plural, definite force, as in several Qurʾanic and Arabic examples; here it can mean trees generally.
rows.anchor: وفي البحر أن هذا مما وقع فيه المفرد موقع الجمع والنكرة موقع المعرفة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the singular شجرة unfolds the trees one by one until not a single tree of the species remains outside the image.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري : إنه قال سبحانه ( شجرة ) على التوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author objects that a lone singular does not normally convey distributive repetition; Arabic expresses that sense by repeating the noun, as in رجلا رجلا.
rows.anchor: وتعقب بأن إفادة المفرد التفصيل بدون تكرار غير معهود والمعهود إفادته ذلك بالتكرير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أقلام is a plural of paucity although the context suggests abundance, because no other familiar plural of قلم is in circulation; قلام is uncommon.
rows.anchor: وإختيار جمع القلة في ( أقلام ( مع أن الأنسب للمقام جمع الكثرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Baḥr most naturally denotes the encircling ocean, the known and greatest single sea; a generic sea is possible, but the known ocean makes the image stronger.
rows.anchor: والبحر ( أي المحيط فأل للعهد لأنه المتبادر ولأنه الفرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من بعده can mean after the ocean's supply is exhausted, or alternatively from behind it.
rows.anchor: يمده من بعده ( اي من بعد نفاذه وقيل من ورائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seven additional seas are imagined as each matching the ocean in extent, encirclement, and water; seven signifies abundance rather than exactly seven.
rows.anchor: سبعة أبحر ( مفروضة كل منها مثله في السعة والإحاطة وكثرة الماء والمراد بالسبعة الكثرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author adduces the report that a believer eats in one stomach and an unbeliever in seven as an example where seven conveys multiplicity.
rows.anchor: كما في قوله عليه الصلاة والسلام : المؤمن يأكل في معي واحد والكافر يأكل في سبعة أمعاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seven is chosen as a complete and symbolically weighty number, familiar from the heavens, planets, regions, and days of the week; this gives the image more grandeur than seventy.
rows.anchor: وأخاتيرت لها لأنها عدد تام كما عرفت عند الكلام في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أبحر is formally a plural of paucity, fitting the word سبعة, while both are figuratively used for great multiplicity.
rows.anchor: ولما لم تكن موضوعة في الأصل لذلك بل للعدد المعروف القليل جاء تمييزها أبحر بلفظ القلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording يمده evokes continuously replenishing an inkpot: it implies ink without saying مداد and its imperfect form pictures unceasing supply.
rows.anchor: لكن جيء بما في النظم الجليل لأن يمده يغني عن ذكر المداد لأنه من قولك : مد الدواة

words: والبحر يمده من بعده سبعة أبحر
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The image turns the ocean into an inkpot with seven matching seas continually pouring ink into it.
rows.anchor: فأفاد النظم الجليل جعل البحر المحيط بمنزلة الدواة وجعل أبحر سبعة مثله مملوءة مدادا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the preferred parsing, البحر is nominative as subject and يمده is its predicate; the clause is circumstantial, linked by واو الحال to the relative phrase or its pronoun.
rows.anchor: ورفع ( البحر ) على ما أستظهره أبو حيان فيه على الإبتداء وجملة يمده خبره والواو للحال

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī treats such circumstantial nominal clauses as adverbial in meaning, so their relation to the preceding clause resembles a ظرف even without an explicit pronoun.
rows.anchor: وأشار الزمخشري إلى أن هذه الجملة وما أشبهها كقوله : وقد أغتدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author finds the circumstantial link sufficient through واو الحال; he rejects the need to posit a pronoun transferred from an understood adverb.
rows.anchor: نعم الحق أن الربط بالواو كاف عن الضمير ولا يحتاج معه إلى تكلف هذه المؤنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other parses make the circumstantial clause modify الأرض through its sense of established location, or let البحر's ال stand for a pronoun under the Kufan analysis.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن تكون الجملة حالا من الأرض والعامل فيه معنى الإستقرار والرابط ما سمعت

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī's analysis requires من شجرة to explain the pronoun referring to ما, avoiding an unrelated phrase splitting the relative clause.
rows.anchor: قال في الكشف : ولا بد أن يجعل ( من شجرة ) بيانا للضمير

rows.speaker: الطيبي
rows.claim: Al-Ṭībī says that if ال substitutes for the pronoun annexed to الأرض, البحر generalizes to all seas and makes the seven seas separate from Earth's sea.
rows.anchor: وقال الطيبي : إن البحر على ذلك يعم جميع الأبحر لقرينة الإضافة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author sees no real distinction between the analyses and favors the familiar ocean: annexation most naturally marks definiteness, and that ocean encircles the whole Earth.
rows.anchor: ورد بأنه لا فرق بينهما بل كون بحرها للعهد أظهر لأن العهد أصل الإضافة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī also permits البحر to coordinate with the syntactic sense of أن and its complement, with يمده as a circumstantial clause.
rows.anchor: وجوز الزمخشري كون رفعه بالعطف على محل أن ومعمولها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author objects that coordinating across the elided predicate's evidential trigger makes the omitted verb's relation to the coordinate unclear; a reply allows more freedom in a dependent coordinate.
rows.anchor: وتعقب بأن الدال على الفعل المحذوف هو أن وخبره على ما قرر في بابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the coordination analysis, البحر coordinates with the singular verbal noun that serves as subject of ثابت, not with an entire sentence.
rows.anchor: إذ الظاهر أن المعطوف عليه إنما هو المصدر الواقع فاعلا لثبت وهو مفرد لا جملة

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: A subject-first analysis would put an overt noun directly after conditional لو, which Abu Hayyan allows only as poetic necessity, citing a verse about thirst.
rows.anchor: إذ يصير التقدير ولو البحر وذلك على ما قال أبو حيان لا يجوز إلا في ضرورة شعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another proposal makes البحر a subject, treats the clause as a predicate with واو المعية, and puts the whole clause in the accusative as a مفعول معه; the author calls it far-fetched.
rows.anchor: وجوز كون الرفع على الإبتداء وجملة ( يمده ) خبر المبتدأ والواو واو المعية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A proposed independent answer to an imagined question about the ink is rejected because beginning an answer with واو is not established in this use.
rows.anchor: وجوز كون الواو على ذلك للإستئناف بياني كأنه قيل : ما المداد حينئذ فقيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author also dismisses the claim that واو introduces an answer to a debating question, judging that grammatical defense unreliable.
rows.anchor: وتعقب بأن اقتران الجواب بالواو وإن كانت إستئنافية غير معهود

rows.speaker: البصريان
rows.claim: The two Basran readers pronounce البحر in the accusative, coordinating it with the noun of أن; يمده then predicates that the sea is replenished by seven seas.
rows.anchor: وقرأ البصريان ( والبحر ) بالنصب على أنه معطوف على أسم أن

rows.speaker: ابن الحاجب
rows.claim: Ibn al-Ḥājib rejects taking يمده as a circumstantial clause because that restricts an inanimate subject and leaves البحر without a predicate; أقلام already predicates the first noun.
rows.anchor: قال إبن الحاجب في أماليه : ولا يستقيم أن يكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another parse makes the accusative البحر coordinate with the omitted verb ثابت under لو, leaving يمده without a syntactic position.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن يكون منصوبا على شريطة التفسير عطفا على الفعل المحذوف أعني ثبت

rows.speaker: عبدالله
rows.claim: ʿAbd Allāh reads وبحر as an indefinite nominative; Ibn Jinnī supplies an omitted predicate, while the author says يمده can straightforwardly be its predicate.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عبدالله ( وبحر ) بالتنكير والرفع وخرج ذلك إبن جني على أنه مبتدأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On ʿAbd Allāh's reading, the author prefers making يمده the predicate of the indefinite subject, with no need to posit an omitted predicate.
rows.anchor: والظاهر على تقدير كونه مبتدأ جعل الجملة خبره ولا حاجة إلى جعل خبره محذوفا

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود وأبي
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd and Ubayy read تمده with feminine تاء, from mad, as in the common reading.
rows.anchor: وقرأ إبن مسعود وأبي ( تمده ) بتاء التأنيث

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود والحسن وابن مصرف وابن هرمز
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd, al-Ḥasan, Ibn Muṣarrif, and Ibn Hurmuz read يمده with a ḍamma on ياء, from the causative امداد.
rows.anchor: وقرأ إبن مسعود أيضا والحسن وإبن مصرف وإبن هرمز ( يمده ) بضم الياء التحتية

rows.speaker: ابن الشيخ
rows.claim: Ibn al-Shaykh says the forms يمدّ and يُمدّ are two dialect variants with the same meaning.
rows.anchor: قال إبن الشيخ : يمد بفتح فضم ويمد بضم فكسر لغتان بمعنى

rows.speaker: جعفر بن محمد
rows.claim: Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad reads والبحر مداده, meaning the ink with which one writes; Ibn ʿAṭiyya identifies مداد as a verbal noun.
rows.anchor: وقرأ جعفر بن محمد رضي الله تعالى عنهما ( والبحر مداده ) أي ما يكتب به من الحبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما نفدت كلمات الله is the جواب لو; an omitted scenario is understood from context, a concise ellipsis contrasting unbounded divine words with finite pens and ink.
rows.anchor: ما نفدت كلمات الله ( جواب ( لو ) وفي الكلام إختصار يسمى حذف إيجاز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the trees became pens and the sea plus seven seas became ink and wrote God's words, the words would not run out, while the pens and ink would.
rows.anchor: وكتبت بتلك الأقلام وبذلك المداد كلمات الله تعالى ما نفدت لعدم تناهيها ونفد تلك الأقلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author compares the omitted wording to the concise ellipsis in the expiation verse: if one shaved the head to remove harm, then expiation is due.
rows.anchor: ونظير ذلك في الإشتمال على إيجاز الحذف قوله تعالى : ( أؤ به أذى من رأسه ففدية )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the interpretation tied to the reported occasion, God's words mean His knowledge and wisdom; this reading answers the question about how much knowledge people received.
rows.anchor: والمراد بكلماته تعالى كلمات علمه سبحانه وحكمته جل شأنه وهو الذي يقتضيه سبب النزول

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: ʿIkrima reports that the People of the Book asked the Prophet about the spirit, then objected that the claim of little knowledge conflicted with the Torah's wisdom; this verse was revealed in reply.
rows.anchor: أخرج إبن جرير عن عكرمة قال : سأل أهل الكتاب رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم عن الروح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account has Jews ask the Prophet directly, suggesting a Medinan setting; another has Jews instruct a Quraysh delegation, which supports a Meccan setting.
rows.anchor: وظاهر هذا أن اليهود قالوا ذلك له عليه الصلاة والسلام مشافهة وهو ظاهر في أن الآية مدنية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further narrative places the spirit question in Mecca and a later challenge by Jewish scholars after the migration; the Prophet answers that Torah knowledge is little beside God's knowledge and that wisdom is much good.
rows.anchor: وفي رواية أنه نزل بمكة قوله تعالى : ( ويسألونك )

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes God's words as His decreed acts and wonders, brought into being by كن فيكون; calling them words uses cause for effect.
rows.anchor: وقيل : المراد بها مقدوراته جل وعلا وعجائبه عزوجل

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: The Imam prefers the decreed acts and wonders interpretation because it more clearly follows the preceding statement that everything in heaven and earth belongs to God, then signals the unbounded scope of His dominion.
rows.anchor: وهذا ما أختاره الإمام في المراد بكلماته تعالى إلا أن في إنطباقه على سبب النزول خفاء

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abū Muslim understands the words as God's promised reward for obedience and threatened punishment for disobedience, showing that more of His dominion remains unseen than has appeared.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي مسلم المراد بها ما وعد سبحانه به أهل طاعته من الثواب وما أوعد جل شأنه به أهل معصيته

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda reports that polytheists said the revelation would soon run out; the verse answers them, although this reading has a weak connection to the surrounding verses.
rows.anchor: بناء على ما أخرج عبدالرزاق وإبن جرير وإبن المنذر وغيرهم عن قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine sound plural كلمات is formally a plural of paucity, implying that even a small number of God's words cannot be exhausted, let alone a great number.
rows.anchor: وإيثار الجمع المؤنث السالم بناء على أنه كجمع المذكر جمع قلة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads ما نفد كلام الله without feminine تاء and uses the singular كلام instead of كلمات.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن ( ما نفد ) بغير تاء ( كلام الله ) بدل كلمات الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing attributes explain why God's words cannot be exhausted: nothing can overcome Him, and nothing falls outside His knowledge and wisdom.
rows.anchor: إن الله عزيز ( لا يعجزه جل شأنه شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: قل is a reply to the deniers: tell them that the Angel of Death takes them.
rows.anchor: يستوفي نفوسكم لا يترك منها شيئا من أجزائها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يتوفاكم means to take the souls in full, leaving no part behind, or to take every one of them so that none remains alive; the root sense is taking something completely.
rows.anchor: يستوفي نفوسكم لا يترك منها شيئا من أجزائها أولا يترك شيئا من جزئياتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author explains توفي through استيفاء, noting that the patterns تفعّل and استفعال often overlap in meaning.
rows.anchor: وأصل التوفي أخذ الشيء بتمامه وفسر بالإستيفاء لأن التفعل والإستفعال يلتقيان كثيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Death is attributed to the Angel of Death because he directly takes souls by God's command; being assigned to people means he takes their souls and knows their lifespans.
rows.anchor: ونسبة التوفي إلى ملك الموت بإعتبار أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام يباشر قبض الأنفس بأمره عزوجل

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر محمد بن علي
rows.claim: Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī reports that the Prophet visited a sick Anṣārī with the Angel of Death at his head; the angel said he is gentle with believers, visits every household five times daily, and cannot take even a mosquito without God's order.
rows.anchor: وأخرج إبن أبي حاتم وأبو الشيخ عن أبي جعفر محمد بن علي رضي الله تعالى عنهما قال : دخل رسول الله

rows.speaker: الطبراني وأبو نعيم وابن منده
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarānī, Abū Nuʿaym, and Ibn Mandah are said to transmit a similar report about the Angel of Death.
rows.anchor: وأخرج نحوه الطبراني وأبو نعيم وإبن منده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God the one who takes souls attributes the act to Him as creator of human acts, with no creaturely agency beyond acquisition according to Ashʿarīs, or because the act occurs by God's permission and will.
rows.anchor: ونسبته إليه عزوجل في قوله سبحانه : ( الله يتوفى الأنفس ) بإعتبار أن أفعال العباد كلها مخلوقة له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking souls is also attributed to messengers and angels because the Angel of Death has helpers who draw out the soul; he takes it when its departure is near.
rows.anchor: ونسبته إلى الرسل في قوله تعالى : ( توفته رسلنا ) وإلى الملائكة في قوله سبحانه

rows.speaker: أبو أمامة
rows.claim: Abū Umāma reports the Prophet saying that God assigned the Angel of Death to take souls, except martyrs at sea, whose souls God takes Himself.
rows.anchor: أخرج إبن ماجه عن أبي أمامة قال : سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول إن الله تعالى وكل ملك الموت

rows.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk reports from Ibn ʿAbbās that separate angels take the souls of humans, jinn, devils, birds, wild animals, beasts, fish, and ants; the Angel of Death later takes angels' souls and then dies.
rows.anchor: أخرج إبن جوبير عن الضحاك عن إبن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما قال : وكل ملك الموت

rows.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: That report says God Himself takes the souls of martyrs at sea as an honor to them, rather than assigning them to the Angel of Death.
rows.anchor: وأما الشهداء في البحر فإن الله تعالى يلي قبض أرواحهم لا يكل ذلك إلى ملك الموت

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority hold that one Angel of Death takes the souls of rational and nonrational creatures; he is called ʿAzrāʾīl, glossed as servant of God, and has helpers.
rows.anchor: والذي ذهب إليه الجمهور أن ملك الموت لمن يعقل وما لا يعقل من الحيوان واحد وهو عزرائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author leaves the soundness of al-Ḍaḥḥāk's report from Ibn ʿAbbās to God's knowledge.
rows.anchor: وخبر الضحاك عن إبن عباس الله تعالى أعلم بصحته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The return to God is resurrection for judgment and recompense.
rows.anchor: ثم إلى ربكم ترجعون 11 ( بالبعث للحساب والجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the preceding context says they denied meeting God's angels at death and what follows it, mentioning the Angel of Death signals that they will meet him, and return to God means resurrection.
rows.anchor: لأنهم لما جحدوا لقاء ملائكة ربهم عند الموت وما يكون بعده ذكر لهم حديث توفي ملك الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the verse answers their denial of resurrection; death is mentioned because resurrection follows death, as a warning and as proof that the one able to cause death can restore life.
rows.anchor: وأما على ما قيل فوجه المناسبة أنهم أنهم لما أنكروا البعث والمعاد رد عليهم بما ذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author calls it a weak interpretation that the verse rebuts a naturalistic account of death inferred from their phrase أئذا ضللنا في الأرض.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إن ذلك لرد ما يشعر به كلامهم من أن الموت بمقتضى الطبيعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author calls still more remote the argument that because ʿAzrāʾīl extracts the soul from the body, the Creator can distinguish bodily parts mixed into earth; the soul's hidden relation was disputed even by rational people.
rows.anchor: وأبعد منه ما قيل في المناسبة : إن عزرائيل وهو عبد من عبيده تعالى إذا قدر على تخليص الروح

rows.speaker: زيد بن علي
rows.claim: Zayd ibn ʿAlī reads ترجعون in the active voice.
rows.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي رضي الله تعالى عنهما ( ترجعون ) بالبناء للفاعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: المجرمون may mean the people who said أئذا ضللنا في الأرض, or the whole class of criminals to which they belong.
rows.anchor: وهم القائلون : ( أئذا ضللنا في الأرض ) أو جنس المجرمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ناكسوا رؤوسهم means lowering their heads in shame and disgrace.
rows.anchor: ناكسوا رؤوسهم ( مطرقوها من الحياء والخزي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are before their Lord at judgment, when the ugly deeds they committed in worldly life are exposed.
rows.anchor: عند ربهم ( حين حسابهم لما يظهر من قبائحهم التي أقترفوها في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The quoted plea is an utterance understood as a circumstantial clause governed by ناكسوا; this is better than supplying يستغيثون بقولهم.
rows.anchor: ومفعولا ربنا بتقدير القول الواقع حالا والعامل فيه ( ناكسوا )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They now perceive visible and audible signs and have the capacity to apprehend them, whereas before they were blind and deaf in the sense of failing to perceive anything.
rows.anchor: أي صرنا ممن يبصر ويسمع وحصل لنا الإستعداد لإدراك الآيات المبصرة والآيات المسموعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They beg to be returned to worldly life so they can act righteously in light of the signs.
rows.anchor: وهذا على ما قيل إدعاء منهم لصحة مشعري البصر والسمع

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One explanation is that the plea claims their faculties of sight and hearing are now sound.
rows.anchor: وهذا على ما قيل إدعاء منهم لصحة مشعري البصر والسمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إنا موقنون may resume and explain the preceding plea, or stand as a resumption without intended causal force; either way it claims sound hearts and capacity to understand signs and act on them.
rows.anchor: إنا موقنون 21 ( إستئناف لتعليل ما قبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their declaration displays firmness in certainty and eagerness for it, which may explain why they do not add وأيقنا to أبصرنا وسمعنا.
rows.anchor: وفيه من إظهار الثبات على الإيقان وكمال رغبتهم فيه ما فيه وكأنه لذلك لم يقولوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sight precedes hearing because most promised righteous action follows hearing, so placing hearing last avoids interrupting that connection.
rows.anchor: ولعل تأخير السمع لأن أكثر العمل الصالح الموعود يترتب عليه دون البصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One proposed sense is that they saw the resurrection they denied and its promised consequences, and heard the divine questioning of humans and jinn about messengers warning them of this day.
rows.anchor: بأن يقال : أبصرنا بالبعث الذي كنا ننكره وما وعدتنا به على إنكاره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another proposed sense is that they saw the resurrection and heard the messengers' words, now hearing them obediently and acknowledging them.
rows.anchor: أو يقال أبصرنا البعث وسمعنا قول الرسل أي سمعناه سمع طاعة وإذعان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further proposal is that they saw the ugliness of deeds they once considered good and heard angels tell them they would return to the Fire.
rows.anchor: قبح أعمالنا التي كنا نراها في الدنيا حسنة وسمعنا قول الملائكة لنا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says they saw God's messengers and heard their speech while still in worldly life.
rows.anchor: وقيل : أرادوا أبصرنا رسلك وسمعنا كلامهم حين كنا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further view says they saw God's creative signs and heard revealed signs in worldly life, admitting that God had proof against them; the author calls this reading weak.
rows.anchor: أو أبصرنا آياتك التكوينية وسمعنا آياتك التنزيلية في الدنيا فلك الحجة علينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second-person address is phrased singularly but applies to every person capable of seeing.
rows.anchor: والخطاب في : ترى لكل واحد ممن يصح منه الرؤية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The horror would astonish any observer, even one used to extraordinary sights and calamities.
rows.anchor: إذ المراد بيان كمال سوء حالهم وبلوغها من الفظاعة إلى حيث لا يختص إستغرابها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation is that their state is so manifest that it cannot be hidden, so no particular observer is singled out.
rows.anchor: وقيل : لأن القصد إلى بيان أن حالهم قد بلغت من الظهور إلى حيث يمتنع خفاؤها البتة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says the estimated answer fits the first explanation about universal astonishment better; ترى is intransitive, with no expressed object.
rows.anchor: والجواب المقدر أوفق بما ذكر أولا والفعل منزل منزلة اللازم فلا يقدر له مفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another parse supplies an object from what follows: لو ترى المجرمين or their lowering of their heads.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن يقدر لترى مفعول دل عليه ما بعد أي لو ترى المجرمين أو لو ترى نكسهم رؤسهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A view addresses only the Prophet and reads لو as a wish that he could see the criminals, perhaps to rejoice at them; most grammarians say such a wish has no answer.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن يكون الخطاب خاصا بسيد المخاطبين صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: أبو حيان وابن مالك
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan and Ibn Mālik insist that a wish expressed with لو requires an answer, citing al-Muhalhil's line about the buried Kulayb, where they construe لقر جوابا.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حيان وإبن مالك : لا بد لها من الجواب إستدلالا بقول مهلهل في حرب البسوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author replies that al-Muhalhil's لو is conditional, not optative, and يخبر coordinates with an infinitive understood from نبش.
rows.anchor: ورد بأنها شرطية ويخبر عطف على مصدر متصيد من نبش

rows.speaker: الخفاجي
rows.claim: Al-Khafājī offers a simpler account: when لو often carries a wish, it can take the wish construction's ruling, allowing omission of an unexpressed answer and an accusative answer.
rows.anchor: وقال الخفاجي عليه الرحمة : لو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The past forms in the counterfactual and إذ suit an event already realized in God's eternal knowledge, expressed as past by figurative usage.
rows.anchor: والمضي في لو الإمتناعية وإذ لأن أخباره تعالى عما تحقق في علمه الأزلي لتحققه بمنزلة الماضي

rows.speaker: أبو العباس
rows.claim: Abū al-ʿAbbās unusually reads the sentence as part of the command to say: Tell Muḥammad, if you could see the criminals; Abū Ḥayyān explains that he links it to يتوفاكم under the earlier قل.
rows.anchor: ومن الغريب قول أبي العباس في الآية : المعنى قل يامحمد للمجرم ولو ترى
